sources.entry: Tequila - A native macOS productivity app integrating Focus, Timer, Calendar, Unified Mail, and Logs.

summary.one_liner: Tequila is a native macOS productivity workspace, written in Swift with SwiftUI and AppKit, that combines task management, timers, a calendar, multi-account email, settings, and notes in one app.
summary.what_it_does: Tequila is organized into six modules: Focus, Timer, Calendar, Mail, Settings, and Logs. Focus holds tasks with completion status, the ability to hide tasks without deleting them, count-up and countdown day counters, weekday-based fixed scheduling, an All Day option, and export of daily task info. Timer offers count-up and countdown timers with projects organized into folders. Calendar lets you customize colors, typography, and highlights and export monthly views. Mail is a central interface for several email services, named as Gmail, Outlook, iCloud Mail, Proton Mail, Yahoo Mail, 163 Mail, and QQ Mail. Settings covers backgrounds, colors, typography, and a configurable region shown in the upper-right corner. Logs holds notes, research, and reference material in folders, with text, images, and tables.
use_cases: plan my week with recurring weekday tasks
track elapsed or remaining days to an event
time focused work sessions with count-up or countdown timers
check multiple email accounts in one app
keep organized notes and research on a Mac
customize a calendar view and export it
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank in its clone command)
Open the project in Xcode to explore the source code
Alternatively, download a build from the GitHub Releases page
notable: Six integrated modules (tasks, timers, calendar, mail, settings, notes) in a single native macOS workspace
Weekday-based fixed scheduling with per-day removal and an All Day option
Count-up and countdown day counters for date tracking
Mail module covering several named email providers, including 163 Mail and QQ Mail
Release history from v1.0 to v1.6 documented in the README
caveats: Built specifically for macOS; no other platforms are mentioned
The README's clone command has no repository URL filled in
Xiaohongshu engagement figures in the README are self-reported and not verified downloads or users
